result.title: RL Can Only Reinforce What It Sees Succeed
result.summary: When a familiar rule stops working, an agent has to weigh what pre-training taught it against what it now observes. We ask how outcome-reward reinforcement learning (RL) changes this balance, in a puzzle world where both sides are known: small language models trained from scratch on games played by a Bayesian player, so that the prior and the right answer are exact. Base models hedge as their corpus did, and RL turns that hedging into decisions, in whichever direction the reward favours. But RL can only reinforce what it sees succeed. When the right action is rare, each run either learns it everywhere or not at all, and which runs take off is predicted before training by one count: the expected number of groups of attempts in which the action wins. About 35 such groups give even odds. The count holds for new and repeated problems and for groups of 4 to 256 attempts, and across learning rates, optimizers, GRPO variants and model sizes from 1.3M to 85M parameters, which move the threshold but not what is counted.

AI.brief_summary: 研究小语言模型在贝叶斯先验与观测冲突的谜题环境中，outcome-reward RL 如何改变二者的权衡；发现「预期成功组数」这一训练前计数可预测学习是否发生，约 35 组成功样本才达到均等概率，且该计数跨问题、组大小与优化器稳定。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 轨迹训练中的成功采样覆盖和贡献分配相关，可能提示稀有正确推理路径能否被 group 采样命中会决定训练成败，可供核查该阈值是否适用于多模态推理轨迹的监督设计。
